newsitem.title: POLAND: Clinton hails Poland's prospective entry into NATO.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails Poland's prospective entry into NATO.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton congratulated Poland on Thursday on its prospective entry into NATO, saying "Poland is coming home" eight years after the fall of Soviet-dominated communism there.

Addressing a crowd of thousands in historic Castle Square in a section of Warsaw raised from the rubble of World War Two, Clinton said Poland was being restored to the community of democracies "and to the destiny you deserve."

Clinton came to Warsaw straight from Madrid, where he and other NATO leaders earlier this week agreed to invite Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to join the world's most powerful security alliance. They said the door would remain open to others, including Romania and Slovenia.

"Now Poland is joining NATO. Poland is taking its place in the community of democracy. Never again will your fate be decided by others. Never again will the birthright of freedom be denied you. Poland is coming home," the U.S. leader said.
Clinton coupled his congratulatory rhetoric with sober words about the responsibilities of NATO membership.

"We know you are ready to share the burdens of defending freedom, because you know the price of losing freedom," he said, referring to Poland's tragic history of foreign invasion and repression throughout much of the 20th century and before.
